name: chat.startStream

channel.desc: An encoded ID that represents a channel, thread, or DM.

chunks.desc: Array of streaming chunks. Can include markdown text chunk objects, task update chunk objects, plan update chunks, or blocks chunks.

markdown_text.desc: Accepts message text formatted in markdown. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.

thread_ts.desc: Provide another message's ts value to reply to. Omit it to stream a top-level message instead of a thread reply; this is only supported in channels where the whole channel is one session, such as Slack Code, and returns invalid_thread_ts elsewhere. Passing "0" is equivalent to omitting it.

recipient_user_id.desc: The encoded ID of the user to receive the streaming text. Required when streaming to channels.

recipient_team_id.desc: The encoded ID of the team the user receiving the streaming text belongs to. Required when streaming to channels.

task_display_mode.desc: Specifies how tasks are displayed in the message. timeline task updates render as individual task cards interleaved with streamed text. plan task updates render together in a plan block.

icon_emoji.desc: Emoji to use as the icon for this message. Overrides icon_url.

icon_url.desc: Image URL to use as the icon for this message.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
